title: Cost a recipe whose ingredients are recipes

blocks.text: A bakery's costing tool works out what each item on the menu costs to make. A recipe's cost is the sum of its ingredients' costs, and an ingredient can be a recipe of its own: the pesto in pasta al pesto. Working an item out is slow in the real tool, so each cost is worked out once and remembered in the `known` map.
Write `cost(item)` in `src/main/java/practice/RecipeCosts.java`. `workOut(item)` already computes a cost from scratch, calling `cost(...)` for each ingredient.
When you're done, any item can be costed, whatever has or hasn't been costed before it, and no item is worked out twice. About five lines.

cases.says: a raw ingredient costs its price, on every lookup
a recipe whose ingredients, and sub-recipes, have never been costed gets the sum of their costs
an item whose cost is known is not worked out again, including when it is an ingredient of another recipe

origin.section: Spot the Problem: a Price Memo That Fails Only When a Bundle's Parts Are Unpriced

concepts: A computeIfAbsent mapping function must not modify its own map; HashMap throws ConcurrentModificationException when a nested call inserts, so a memo fails only when the nested item is new.
